pull_request.body:
**Scope:**
This PR updates `src/security-validator.ts` by removing `@test.com` patterns from the placeholder allowlist to enforce that placeholder emails properly use the `@example.` domain, adhering to RFC 2606.

**Validation:**
- Ran `npm test` successfully (all 16 security validation tests passed, including new test cases for `@test.com` failing and `@example.com` passing).
- Ran code review via internal review systems.

**Rollback:**
Revert this commit to re-add `@test.com` to the allowed placeholder list. No database or structural migrations are involved.

pull_request.title: chore(state): record diagnostics-first cycle 16 checkpoint
pull_request.body:
## Summary

This checkpoint records diagnostics-first cycle 16 from the existing maintenance workflow. It inventories the current owner-repository scope, captures all current default-branch refs, rechecks prior non-clean pull requests through REST endpoints, and records current blockers without mutating engineering repositories.

## Verified results

- 253 owner repositories and 307 owner-controlled open pull requests were observed.
- Current default-branch refs were captured for all 253 owner repositories with no fetch errors.
- The cycle engine completed without engine errors.
- State JSON validation, the empty-state-branch regression test, the summary-persistence test, and the local diff check passed.
- No engineering-repository commits, pull-request mutations, workflow reruns, rebases, merges, closes, authentication changes, or branch-protection changes were performed.

## Current blockers

- Scope changed from cycle 15 (251 repositories / 301 open pull requests), so trend comparisons are not directly comparable.
- `codex#25` and `codex#48` remain conflicting; `codex#25` has multiple failed or cancelled CI results and `codex#48` has platform failures with in-progress jobs.
- `codex#49` remains unstable with failed CI checks. Newly observed `codex#52` was unstable while checks were still queued or running; no rerun was initiated.
- Maintenance PR5 merged after the cycle-16 engine scan; this was observed through REST and was not performed by the maintenance cycle.
- Review and protection boundaries remain unchanged. No review bypass is authorized.

The checkpoint is intentionally reviewable and does not modify the default branch directly.
